newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee growers declare debt moratorium.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee growers declare debt moratorium.

text.p: A leader of Colombia's independent coffee growers' association, Unidad Cafetera Nacional, said delegates from across the country agreed at a meeting Wednesday to declare a moratorium on debt payments with immediate effect.

The moratorium would affect about $200 million in past-due loans owed to the state-run Caja Agria bank and Banco Cafetero, a bank partly owned by the government-affiliated National Coffee Growers' Federation, said Jorge Enrique Robledo, the Unidad Cafetera's national coordinator.

He said the measure -- which could trigger judicial action and possible moves to confiscate the property of debtors -- was agreed unanimously at a meeting of the Unidad Cafetera in the western city of Pereira.

A total of 650 delegates from 102 coffee-growing regions across the country attended the meeting, where growers also agreed to press for a sharp increase in Colombia's internal coffee price and for government assistance in restructuring their debts.
Colombia's internal coffee price was raised 12 percent to 248,1245 pesos per 125-kg load just last week.
But Robledo said independent growers would insist that the National Coffee Growers' Federation raise it again, to a record- high 290,000 pesos per load.

Growers, who have long complained of their growing impoverishment and a lack of government aid to stop it, will also demand access to new forms of credit since all but a few are "on the blacklists" of Colombia's banks, Robledo said.

Asked what independent growers would do if banks foreclosed on their loans and moved to seize their assets and property, Robledo sadi push could quickly come to shove in Colombia's main coffee-growing regions.
"We're not going to let anyone's land be taken away from them," Robledo told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Government officials and spokesmen for the National Coffee Growers' Federation could not be reached for immediate comment.
